text: An eclipse is a New or Full Moon with extra force, and this one falls in your first house: your physical self, the name you go by, and the impression you make before you have said anything. Eclipses come in seasons about twice a year, and a series works the same pair of houses for a year or two while the lunar nodes pass through, so treat this as a chapter rather than a single day. The chapter's subject is you. During these months, questions of identity speed up. A haircut becomes a new look, a new look becomes a new bearing, and people who have not seen you in a while say you seem different. Solar eclipses here act like amplified New Moons: they open doors, and you may find yourself starting things, stepping forward, or being nudged into visibility before you feel fully ready. Lunar eclipses act like amplified Full Moons: something about how you have been living comes to a head, and you see plainly which version of yourself still fits and which one you have outgrown. Because the first house sits across from the seventh, the same series also lights up your closest relationships, and much of the growth happens in that back and forth: how much of you gets shaped by another person, and how much comes from you. Old self-images tend to fall away quickly under these skies, faster than they would on their own. That can feel abrupt in the moment and obvious in hindsight. The useful posture is a light grip. Start what wants to start, retire the mask that no longer earns its keep, and hold off on final judgments during the eclipse itself, since the meaning of each event usually settles over the following weeks. By the time the series moves on, you often look back and find that your sense of who you are updated more in this stretch than in the several quiet years before it.

For a year or two, the eclipses are working through your second house, which covers earnings, belongings, and the resources you handle in your own name. Since eclipses arrive in seasons roughly twice a year and keep returning to the same axis of houses, this is a running storyline about resources, not one dramatic afternoon. The pace of financial life tends to pick up. A source of income may wind down while another appears, sometimes in the same season. Something you own may leave your hands, or something you have wanted for years may finally arrive. A solar eclipse here carries New Moon character, seeding a fresh chapter: a new way of earning, a new sense of what your work is worth, a first serious attempt at saving or building. A lunar eclipse carries Full Moon character, ripening what was already in motion: a raise or a reckoning, a purchase completed, a clear view of where the money actually goes. Underneath the ledger sits the deeper theme of this house, which is worth. During this series you find out what you genuinely value, often by watching what you fight to keep and what you release with relief. The axis pairs your resources with shared ones, so questions of debt, support, inheritance, or a partner's finances can enter the story from the other side. Little of this needs to be forced. The eclipses do the accelerating; your part is to notice which doors are closing on their own and which are opening. The busiest week of a season is usually also the week when the least is settled, so what feels urgent then often reads differently a month later. By the far end of the run, material life has generally reorganized itself around fewer and truer priorities, and your sense of what you bring is steadier than when it started.

The eclipse series has entered your third house, the district of the chart that handles words, daily traffic, siblings, neighbors, learning, and the constant hum of messages. Twice a year or so an eclipse season opens, and the run of them keeps to one pair of houses for a year or two, so this is best read as a long chapter about how you communicate and connect, written in installments. Life in this chapter gets talkative and quick. Conversations carry more consequence than usual: a chance remark opens a door, a long-avoided talk finally happens, an email lands that changes your week. News arrives in bursts. You may find yourself writing more, studying something new, teaching, or handling a season of paperwork, errands, and short trips that reshapes your ordinary routes. Relationships with siblings, cousins, and neighbors can move noticeably, with old silences breaking or busy contact resuming after years. When a solar eclipse falls here, it behaves like a strong New Moon: a course begins, a project gets its first page, a conversation starts something. When a lunar eclipse falls here, it behaves like a strong Full Moon: a manuscript, a message, or a misunderstanding comes to a head and asks to be resolved. The paired house across the axis is the ninth, so small questions of daily learning keep bumping into large questions of belief, and you may notice your opinions updating faster than usual. The exposure this series brings is mostly about voice. Things you have been meaning to say tend to get said, by you or to you, sooner than planned. Speak with ordinary care, let the flurries pass before drawing conclusions, and treat each installment as one scene rather than the whole story. By the end of the series your mind is usually carrying different questions than it started with, and your way of speaking has grown more direct and more your own.

This eclipse belongs to a series moving through your fourth house, the base of the chart: where you live, who you come from, and the part of your life that has no audience. Because eclipse seasons come around twice a year and stay with one axis of houses for a year or two, the story here unfolds in chapters over many months, and this event is one of them. Domestic life accelerates during such a series. Moves, renovations, arrivals, and departures cluster in these years: a household member comes or goes, a lease ends, a family home changes hands, a parent's situation shifts and asks for your attention. Some developments open doors, like a home you did not think you could have. Others close them, like the quiet end of an old living arrangement that had already run its course. A solar eclipse in this house has New Moon character and tends to plant something: a new address, a new household, a decision to put down roots. A lunar eclipse has Full Moon character and tends to complete something: a long process around family or property reaches its natural conclusion, or a truth about your origins comes into the light. Emotionally, this series digs deeper than the surface events suggest. Family patterns you inherited become visible enough to work with, and your definition of home, the place and the feeling, gets tested and refined. The opposite end of the axis is the tenth house of career, so demands from work and demands from home often trade places in these years, each forcing a clearer answer about where your foundation actually is. Give the process time. A choice about where and how to live tends to look clearer in the quiet months between seasons than in the middle of one. Look back once it has gone by and you are usually more honestly rooted than you were at the start, in a place, in a family arrangement, or simply in yourself.

An eclipse season is visiting your fifth house, and it will keep visiting for a year or two, since eclipses return to the same axis of houses in seasons about twice a year while the nodes move through. The fifth house covers romance, children, creative work, and the pleasures you pursue for their own sake, so this series is a long chapter about joy and what you make. Under these eclipses, the heart's calendar speeds up. Romantic life can change status quickly: an attraction becomes a relationship, a casual arrangement asks to become serious, or a connection that was mostly habit reaches its natural end and frees you both. Questions about children, wanting them, having them, or watching yours enter a new stage, often move to the front during this series. Creative work gets the same acceleration. A project you have circled for years may suddenly demand to be made, and work you have kept private may find its audience before you feel prepared, which is exposure of the kindest sort. The solar eclipses of the series behave like New Moons and open: a first date, a first draft, a pregnancy, a stage. The lunar ones behave like Full Moons and crown: the show goes up, the feeling gets spoken, the answer arrives. Across the axis sits the eleventh house of friends and groups, so the series also tests the line between what you create alone and what you owe your circle, and a friendship can turn romantic or a romance settle into friendship along the way. The invitation of these years is sincerity. Half-hearted pleasures and performances tend to fall away quickly, while whatever you love without pretending gets room to grow. Let the openings open, let the endings finish cleanly, and by the close of the series you usually know far more precisely what delights you, and you have made room in your life to do it.

The current eclipse series is working through your sixth house, the domain of daily work, routines, health habits, and the people you labor alongside. Eclipses travel in seasons, about two a year, and revisit the same axis of houses for a year or two, so think of this as an extended overhaul of your everyday life delivered in installments rather than a single disruptive day. During this chapter, the structure of your days becomes negotiable. Jobs change shape: duties are added or removed, a role ends and a better-fitting one opens, a workplace reorganizes around you, or you leave an arrangement your body had been protesting for months. Colleagues and the texture of working relationships matter more than usual, and so do the small systems, schedules, commutes, and habits, that quietly determine how you feel by evening. Health tends to speak up during this series, not as a sentence but as feedback. Sleep, food, movement, and stress make their costs and benefits unusually visible, and adjustments made now tend to stick because circumstances reinforce them. A solar eclipse here opens: a new job, a new regimen, a new way of organizing the week. A lunar eclipse closes: a project ships, a habit exhausts itself, a long-standing strain finally gets attention. Across the axis lies the twelfth house of rest and retreat, so the series keeps weighing service against depletion, asking what you can sustainably give. Some routines will close like doors behind you, and it helps not to pry them back open out of habit. The steadier response is small and repeated: adjust, observe, adjust again between seasons. What is left when the series finishes is usually a daily life rebuilt around what actually works, a job more honest about its costs, and a body you treat less like a machine and more like a colleague.

Partnership is the headline while the eclipses move through your seventh house, the chart's chamber of marriage, close alliances, contracts, and whoever sits on the other side of an agreement with you. An eclipse is a lunation with unusual weight, and eclipses come in seasons about twice a year, returning to the same pair of houses for a year or two, so this is a relationship chapter told across many months, not a verdict delivered in one night. Under this series, commitments clarify quickly. Couples who have been drifting toward a decision tend to reach it: engagements, moves, formal agreements, or honest partings that had been waiting for courage. Single people often meet someone consequential during these seasons, sometimes with a speed that feels arranged. Business partnerships and contracts belong here too, and they follow the same rhythm: agreements are signed, renegotiated, or allowed to lapse. A solar eclipse in this house opens like a strong New Moon, beginning an alliance or a new phase within one. A lunar eclipse culminates like a strong Full Moon, bringing a bond to a decision point where its real terms become visible. The opposite house is your first, the house of self, so the deeper question of the whole series is balance: where you end and the other person begins, what you have outsourced to partners that belongs to you, and what you have carried alone that could be shared. Others may act as mirrors in these years, showing you your own patterns with uncomfortable clarity. Doors close and open here with unusual efficiency, and the endings, seen later, tend to look like room being made. Avoid forcing resolutions during the most intense week of a season; let each event finish explaining itself. By the end of the series, the alliances still standing tend to be the ones that were actually working, and you meet them more as an equal than you did before.

Your eighth house is hosting the eclipses for a while, and its subject matter is entanglement: money that belongs to more than one person, what is owed and what is left behind, real closeness, and the psychological material people usually keep in the basement. Eclipse seasons arrive about twice a year and work one axis of houses for a year or two, so this is a slow excavation in installments, not a single shock. The practical face of this series usually involves other people's resources. Loans are taken or retired, taxes and estates get settled, a partner's financial situation changes and changes yours with it, support is offered or withdrawn. Arrangements built on unspoken terms tend to get their terms spoken during these seasons, which can be uncomfortable in the moment and stabilizing afterward. The intimate face runs deeper. Bonds that involve real vulnerability, where another person has power in your life and you in theirs, intensify or clarify. Trust is tested and often confirmed; where it fails, the failure comes into the open where it can finally be dealt with. A solar eclipse here initiates: a merging of resources, a new depth in a relationship, the first honest look at an old fear. A lunar eclipse settles: a debt is cleared, a secret surfaces, a long grief completes its work. Across the axis sits your second house of personal resources, so the series keeps asking what is yours, what is theirs, and what is genuinely ours. The exposure this chapter brings is mostly relief in disguise, since what stays buried costs energy to keep buried. Paperwork and promises made in the thick of a season often read differently later, and the quieter months in between are where most of the integrating happens anyway. When the whole run is behind you, you tend to travel lighter: fewer entanglements, cleaner agreements, and a steadier relationship with the parts of yourself you used to avoid.

With the eclipse series running through your ninth house, the horizon itself becomes the story. This is where the chart keeps distance and meaning: travel that takes you far from home, advanced study, law, publication, and the framework you use to make sense of everything else. Eclipse seasons come about twice a year, and this one belongs to a run that will hold a single axis of houses for a year or two, so developments here tend to arrive in sequence, each building on the last. Travel and distance often figure literally. A trip planned for years finally happens, an opportunity abroad appears, a connection to another country or culture opens a door you did not know existed. Education follows the same current: degrees begin or conclude, a course of study changes direction, teaching opportunities arrive, something you wrote finds a publisher or a public. Legal matters, where they exist, tend to move toward resolution during these seasons rather than sitting still. The quieter action is in your convictions. Beliefs you inherited or adopted young get tested against experience, and some do not survive the test, which feels less like loss and more like outgrowing a coat. A solar eclipse here starts in New Moon fashion: enrollment, departure, a first step into a larger world. A lunar eclipse concludes in Full Moon fashion: graduation, publication, a settled question, a returned traveler. The paired house across the axis is the third, so grand theories keep being checked against daily facts, and conversations close to home often trigger the biggest shifts in worldview. Let your certainties be provisional during this chapter; the series is efficient at retiring ideas that no longer fit and replacing them with ones earned firsthand. By its end, your world is usually larger, your opinions fewer but sturdier, and your sense of what life is for updated by evidence rather than argument.

Career and reputation take center stage while the eclipses work through your tenth house, the highest and most visible point of the chart. An eclipse is a supercharged New or Full Moon, and since a season of them comes about twice a year, with the whole run staying on one axis of houses for a year or two, your professional life is in an extended chapter of acceleration, this event being one scene in it. Under this series, public standing moves faster than usual in both directions of change. Promotions, title changes, launches, and recognitions cluster in these years, and so do departures: a role you have outgrown ends, a boss or company changes, a professional identity you worked hard to build starts to feel like clothing that no longer fits. Doors close and open with unusual speed, and the closures, in retrospect, tend to look like redirection rather than loss. Visibility itself increases. More people see your work, your name travels further than you push it, and both praise and scrutiny arrive sooner than they used to. Solar eclipses at the top of the chart begin things: a new position, a new ambition, a public debut. Lunar eclipses culminate: a long effort pays off, a professional situation reaches its truth, an achievement or an ending becomes official. The other end of the axis is your fourth house of home and family, so these years keep weighing the climb against the ground you stand on, and events in one arena reliably ripple into the other. The useful discipline is to let your ambitions be examined. Goals adopted to please parents, teachers, or an earlier version of you tend to dissolve under eclipse light, while the work that is genuinely yours gains momentum. Once the series has passed, you are more often in a role that fits, aimed at something you actually want, and visible in a way that needs less managing.

Friendship, community, and whatever you and your people are collectively aiming at: that is the terrain of your eleventh house, and the eclipses are moving through it now. Their seasons come about twice a year. A run of them stays with one axis of houses for a year or two before moving along, so the changes here unfold as a series of chapters rather than a single event. Your social world is the first thing to accelerate. New people arrive who fit the person you are becoming, often through groups, causes, teams, or scenes you had not planned to join. At the same time, some long-standing friendships reach their natural end or change form, which can ache even when both of you sense it is right. Groups you belong to reorganize: you may step into a leading role in one, leave another, or discover that a community you drifted into has become central to your life. The second theme is the future itself. The eleventh house holds your hopes, the long plans that orient your choices, and under eclipse light those plans get audited. Wishes you have carried since an earlier era of your life may quietly expire, replaced by aims that fit current evidence about who you are. Solar eclipses here open in New Moon style: a new circle, a new alliance, a goal named out loud for the first time. Lunar eclipses close in Full Moon style: a group effort bears fruit, a friendship reaches its truth, an old dream is honorably retired. The paired fifth house keeps personal joy in the equation, asking that your networks serve your delight and not only your obligations. Through it all, notice who shows up. The people still around at the close of a series like this often turn out to belong to the chapter after it, and by then your picture of the future is usually both humbler and far more genuinely yours.

This eclipse falls in your twelfth house, the part of the chart that keeps no audience: sleep and dreams, withdrawal, closed institutions, and the backstage of the psyche where things live before and after they are visible. There are roughly two eclipse seasons a year, and a run of them stays with one axis of houses for a year or two, so you are in an extended quiet chapter, and its work is mostly interior. Do not expect the loud, obvious events other houses report. Here the series accelerates what happens below the waterline. Old chapters finish: a long grief completes itself, a habit of mind you have carried for decades loosens, something you have been holding in secret asks to be set down or spoken. Dreams get vivid, memory stirs, and people from the distant past sometimes resurface briefly, as if the psyche were settling accounts. You may feel a stronger than usual need for retreat during these seasons, and honoring it pays, because the insights of this chapter arrive in stillness rather than in traffic. Behind-the-scenes matters can also move: work done without credit gets quietly noticed, hidden arrangements come to light and resolve, time in hospitals, retreats, or other enclosed worlds may figure for you or for someone you care for. Solar eclipses here plant seeds in the dark, beginnings you will not recognize as beginnings until later. Lunar eclipses bring hidden things to completion, often with a release of feeling that surprises you with how clean it is. The sixth house across the axis keeps daily obligations in the picture, and the recurring lesson is that rest is part of the work, not its opposite. Endings in this house are compost, not failure. When the series moves on, you tend to emerge lighter and clearer, carrying less of the past, and ready for the more visible chapter that follows.

Every month the sky produces a New Moon and a Full Moon, and each one lands somewhere in your chart. This time, one of them has landed directly on one of your natal planets, which turns a routine monthly punctuation mark into a personal appointment. A natal planet is a fixed point in you: a set of drives, needs, and talents you have carried since birth. When a lunation hits such a point, the month's weather plugs straight into that circuit, and life around that planet's themes gets busy. Events feel less random than usual, more addressed to you by name. A New Moon on one of your planets behaves like a starting gun for that part of your nature. Something begins there: an opportunity, a meeting, an idea, a first step in a matter that planet has always governed for you. The beginnings are often small at first, a seed rather than a tree, and their importance shows over the following weeks as the cycle unfolds. A Full Moon on one of your planets brings that part of you to a head instead. Something ripens or comes to light: a result lands, a feeling that has been building demands expression, a situation involving that side of your character reaches a point of full visibility where you can finally see it whole. Either way, you tend to feel these lunations physically and emotionally more than the ordinary ones, a kind of inner weather that peaks within a day or two of the exact moment. There is nothing to fix here and nothing to fear. The month is simply speaking directly to a part of you it usually only brushes past. Pay attention to what stirs, act on what feels genuinely ready, and let the rest of the cycle carry the development forward; what starts or culminates now tends to matter more than its size suggests.

An eclipse has landed on one of your natal planets, and this is the moment an eclipse season stops being background weather and becomes personal. Eclipses are the year's strongest lunations, arriving in seasons about twice a year, and most of them touch your chart only in a general way. When one falls directly on a planet of yours, the series has found a live wire: a permanent part of your character, with all its needs and talents, is now wired into a fast-moving story. The signature experience is events that feel aimed. Out of nowhere, the phone rings, the offer appears, the situation shifts, and it lands squarely in the territory that planet has always governed in your life. People often describe an uncanny precision to it, as if the development knew exactly where to find them. What actually happens is acceleration: growth in that area of life that might otherwise have taken years arrives compressed into months. Doors close there, sometimes before you were ready to shut them, and other doors open, sometimes before you knew you wanted them. If it is a solar eclipse, the emphasis is beginnings, a genuinely new chapter starting for that side of you. If lunar, the emphasis is culmination, something long in motion reaching its full expression or its honest end. Because the series revisits the region for a year or two, the story usually develops in installments; the first hit states the theme and later seasons carry it forward. The wisest stance is engaged patience. Say yes to what clearly opens, release what clearly finishes, and postpone irreversible choices made in the heat of the exact week, since the meaning keeps clarifying afterward. Looking back, these are the passages people point to when they explain how they became themselves, and what felt at the time like a hard shove usually reads later as growth.
